techniques.name: Percussive Tribal Acoustic Groove
techniques.description: Driving 16th-note acoustic strumming with palm-muted chucks on beats 2 and 4, creating a relentless pulse that mirrors traditional indigenous rhythms

sequence: Establish a relentless 112 BPM acoustic drive
Keep the picking hand moving in continuous down-up strokes
Drop the fleshy part of your palm lightly onto the strings for percussive slaps
Emphasize the major D chord in the chorus for the Dorian lift
tips: Use a rigid medium-heavy pick (0.80mm) to get a sharp percussive 'crack'
Accent the open A string on beat 1 for heavy bass foundation
Listen to how Shane Howard locks with the kick drum and didgeridoo
details.progression: Am - G - F - G (Verse) / Am - C - D - Am (Chorus)

techniques.name: Dorian Modal Shift & Anthemic Rock Strumming
techniques.description: Transitioning from dark, minor-pentatonic verse chugging into the soaring, defiant Australian rock chorus by highlighting the bright major IV chord (D major), representing the classic A Dorian mode

notes: Dorian major 6th: F# note in the D major chord (2nd fret high E string) lifting the A minor tonality
Chorus progression: Am (X-0-2-2-1-0) to C (X-3-2-0-1-0) to D (X-X-0-2-3-2)
Dynamic attack: Full-bodied open acoustic strumming with strong downbeats
sequence: Build picking intensity as the verse ends on the G major chord
Hit the Am downbeat entering the chorus with full acoustic power
Step into C major, then emphasize the open D chord with high ringing treble
Cycle back to Am to anchor the anthemic 'Standing on sacred ground' hook
tips: Accentuate the F# note on the high E string during the D major chord to bring out the Dorian character
Keep the right hand in continuous down-up 16th-note pendulum motion
Sing along with the chorus hook while maintaining steady acoustic rhythm

beginner.title: Master the Verse Chord Changes
steps: Learn open Am, G, and C chords
Practice moving between Am, G, and F at 90 BPM
Master the chorus progression (Am - C - D - Am)

intermediate.title: Develop Tribal Percussive Groove
steps: Incorporate palm-muted chucks on beats 2 and 4
Clean up the rapid shift into open D major during the chorus
Lock into the relentless 16th-note strumming momentum

advanced.title: Authentic Australian Heritage Performance
steps: Deliver Shane Howard's passionate vocal delivery
Coordinate the rhythm pulse with stompbox or foot-tapping
Perform complete arrangement with commanding presence

commonMistakes: Dragging the tempo — this song needs steady, relentless 112 BPM drive
Playing D minor instead of D major in the chorus (the major D gives the essential Dorian lift)
Strumming too loosely and losing the percussive attack
practiceRoutine: 5 minutes: Percussive strumming drill on muted strings
5 minutes: Verse progression (Am - G - F - G) at 112 BPM
5 minutes: Chorus Dorian transition (Am - C - D - Am)
focusAreas: Clean Dorian D major chord in the chorus
metronomeWork: Practice at 95 BPM with clicks on all four beats
Advance to target 112 BPM once strumming is solid
Set metronome on beats 2 and 4 to lock in the backbeat chuck
